title: Meter burst usage and export to billing pipeline (GPU-seconds + tokens)
author: Nadia Rahman
body:
Summary: Implements first-pass burst usage metering and export to the billing pipeline. This PR introduces a per-tenant burst usage record emitted from the data plane when a request is admitted into burst capacity, along with reconciliation hooks to validate exported usage against admission/controller counters.

Motivation: Dedicated Burst is a paid option; we need durable, auditable usage signals that (a) can be reconciled and (b) are safe to emit at scale (bounded cardinality, no prompt/user payload).

What this PR does: Adds a BurstUsageRecord schema (tenant_id, deployment_id, region, hardware_class, pool_id, request_id, admitted_capacity_class, burst_gpu_ms, burst_tokens, start_ts, end_ts, exporter_version); Emits records only when admitted_capacity_class=BURST and the request actually runs on burst capacity (not merely requested); Introduces a bounded, async exporter that batches records and sends them to the billing ingestion topic (billing.usage.v1) with backpressure and drop accounting; Adds idempotency plumbing (request_id + exporter_version) as a placeholder for downstream de-dupe (full de-dupe and retry-safe semantics are tracked separately); Adds reconciliation hooks: a periodic job that compares (1) admission-controller burst_admitted_gpu_ms_total and (2) billing-exported burst_gpu_ms by tenant/region/hw over a sliding window; logs diffs and emits a reconciliation metric for alerting; Adds feature flag BILLING_BURST_METERING_EXPORT_ENABLED (default OFF) and per-tenant allowlist guard to safely dogfood.

Definitions (important): burst_gpu_ms = wall-clock GPU milliseconds attributed to burst capacity only (baseline GPU time is excluded); burst_tokens = output tokens generated while running on burst capacity; Requests that queue and later run on baseline are not counted; Requests denied burst (and served on baseline via fallback) emit no burst record.

Out of scope / follow-ups: End-to-end de-duplication on retries (downstream + gateway idempotency); Customer-facing line item naming/packaging; Backfill tooling.

Testing: Unit tests for record construction and exporter batching/backpressure; Integration test using in-memory billing sink verifies record emission only under burst admission; Load test sanity: exporter queue stays bounded; metrics show drops when sink is intentionally slowed.

Rollout plan: Keep feature flag OFF; enable for internal dogfood tenants in us-east/H100 first; validate reconciliation diffs <0.5% daily; then expand allowlist per region/hardware per SRE gate.

Notes for reviewers: The billing schema is intentionally minimal; please focus feedback on (a) correctness of what we count as burst and (b) safety/backpressure behavior under sink degradation.

Screens/metrics: Added Grafana panels will land in a separate observability PR; for now see new metrics burst_metering_export_* and burst_reconciliation_diff_ratio in /metrics.

Refs: ENG-4827; ADR semantics for burst admission decisions; Finance asked for GPU-seconds as primary unit with tokens as secondary breakdown.
commits: exporter: add async batching exporter to billing ingestion topic
control-plane: add per-tenant allowlist + feature flag wiring
reconciliation: add sliding-window diff job + metrics
tests: integration coverage for burst-only emission + backpressure
docs: internal notes on schema + operational caveats
review_conversation: Cole Summers (review): Can you clarify whether a request that starts on baseline and then migrates to burst is possible? If yes, how do we handle attribution?

Nadia Rahman (author): Today routing does not migrate an in-flight request between baseline and burst pools; capacity class is fixed per request at dispatch. I added an explicit assertion in record construction to enforce admitted_capacity_class is stable; if we ever add migration, we’ll need segment-level attribution.
Logan Wright (review): Please confirm we are not emitting any high-cardinality labels (request_id) into metrics. Record payload is fine, but metrics must stay bounded.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yep—request_id is only in the exported event. Metrics are aggregated by tenant_id + region + hardware_class + pool_id. Also capped pool_id cardinality via mapping to pool family (e.g., h100-us-east-1a -> h100-us-east).
Ethan Park (review): Where is the feature flag enforced? I want to ensure we can hard-disable export without impacting request path latency.

Nadia Rahman (author): Enforced in router on the emission side (no enqueue), and exporter thread can also be stopped via runtime config. Request path only does a non-blocking tryEnqueue when enabled; disabled is a no-op.
Rishi Malhotra (review): Finance needs GPU-seconds as the billable unit; tokens are helpful but not required. Are GPU-ms computed from actual runtime or allocated capacity?

Nadia Rahman (author): Actual runtime. We measure start/end timestamps around model execution in the burst pool worker and convert to gpu_ms. This is closer to consumption and aligns with how we model cost. Tokens are emitted as an extra dimension for analytics; billing can ignore if needed.
Sean Gallagher (review): What happens when the billing sink is slow/unavailable? Any risk of cascading latency into serving?

Nadia Rahman (author): Export is async with bounded queue. When full, we drop records and increment burst_metering_export_dropped_total with reason=queue_full. Also added reconciliation to detect sustained drops. Serving path never blocks on export.
Cole Summers (review): Requesting one change: please add an explicit 'exporter_version' field so downstream can reason about schema/semantics changes.
Nadia Rahman (author): Done (exporter_version=v1 in this PR).
Cole Summers (approval): Approved after exporter_version addition + minor naming tweaks.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved; thanks for keeping metrics bounded.
Rishi Malhotra (comment): Looks good; please loop Finance when the line item naming is finalized.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved contingent on flag default OFF (confirmed).
notable_snippets: TypeScript (record fields): tenant_id, deployment_id, region, hardware_class, pool_id, request_id, admitted_capacity_class, burst_gpu_ms, burst_tokens, start_ts, end_ts, exporter_version
Exporter behavior: tryEnqueue(record) on request completion; background worker flushes in batches of 200 or every 250ms; drops when queue depth exceeds 10k
Reconciliation: computes diff ratio = abs(admission_gpu_ms - exported_gpu_ms) / max(1, admission_gpu_ms) over 15m windows; emits burst_reconciliation_diff_ratio{tenant,region,hw}
release_notes: Internal: Adds burst usage metering export (flagged off by default) and reconciliation metrics for Dedicated Burst billing readiness.
